notes: Six-MOSFET sheet, 15 components, 9 nets. Layout: a 5V rail across the top (V-DC #0 left lead on the rail, right lead down to GND #1, so the top rail sits at +5V w.r.t. ground); a horizontal rail at y~380; a second horizontal rail at y~462; a bottom ground rail at y~730-755 with GND #14; and a long vertical gate wire at x~365 that runs from the gate of #2 down to the gate of #13. NET MAP: n1 = top rail (y~222-240): V-DC #0 left terminal, drain (top lead) of MOSFET-N #2 via site S2, drain (top lead) of MOSFET-P #3 via site S1, and the top terminal of Zener #4 (the rail's left end turns down at x~75 into the zener). n2 = the x~365 vertical gate wire: gate of MOSFET-N #2 (its lead leaves the gate plate at (408,323) and runs left then down), gate of MOSFET-N #13 (the wire ends at (348,705) and runs right to the gate plate at (437,699)), and the top terminal of V-AC #10 (5V 3kHz) which T's onto it at site S16 - i.e. the 5V/3kHz source drives both gates. n3 = the y~380 rail: source (bottom lead) of MOSFET-P #3, source (bottom lead) of MOSFET-N #2, drain (top lead) of MOSFET-N #6, drain (top lead) of MOSFET-P #5 (the rail's right end turns down at x~674 into #5). n4 = the y~462 rail plus the left column below the zener: bottom terminal of Zener #4, top terminal of V-AC #7 (1V 2kHz), gate of MOSFET-P #3 (site S10), gate of MOSFET-N #6 (the rail ends on the gate plate at (425,470)). n5 = gate of MOSFET-P #5 (right-hand lead, (728,491)) running right along y~492 and down to the top of I-AC #9 (1A 2kHz). n6 = source (bottom lead) of MOSFET-P #5, right end of Resistor #8, drain (top lead) of MOSFET-P #12, joined at site S15. n7 = source (bottom lead) of MOSFET-N #6, left end of Resistor #8 (site S17), drain (top lead) of MOSFET-N #13. n8 = gate of MOSFET-P #12 (right-hand lead) routed right/up to the top of I-AC #11 (5A 3kHz). 0 = ground: V-DC #0 right terminal + GND #1, GND #14, the bottom rail, bottom terminals of V-AC #7, V-AC #10, I-AC #9, I-AC #11, and the sources of #12 and #13. JUDGEMENT CALLS: S6 (374,384) CRITICAL - OVERRIDDEN from the tracer default 'junction' to a crossing, written as explicit edge groups [[13,23],[20,21]] (e13 = up to #2's gate, e23 = down toward S12, e20/e21 = the y~380 rail left and right). The inkmap over y=342..426 shows the gate wire running straight at x~366, swinging right to x~374 exactly at the rail, crossing at y=382-385, then swinging back left to x~366 - a symmetric ~8px lateral excursion, i.e. the drafter's sideways jog meaning 'not connected'. Reading it as a junction (the tracer's default) is what produced the bogus 11-terminal net n3 in the first pass, shorting both gate wires to both rails. S12 (361,462) / S13 (360,469) / S14 (367,469) - the SAME drawn crossing, split by the tracer into three sites where the gate wire jogs around the y~462 rail (inkmap over y=426..506 shows the identical right-then-left excursion). Expressed as S12 = none, S13 = none, S14 = [[23,27,32],[26,31]]: the three arc pieces of the gate wire (e23 above, e27 the arc, e32 below down to S16) form one group, and the two halves of the y~462 rail (e26 left to S10, e31 right to #6's gate) form the other. The 2px skeleton crumbs e29 and e30 carry no terminal and are deliberately left ungrouped. S9 (461,384) CRITICAL -> junction, kept. This is the neighbouring crossing on the same y~380 rail, 87px right of S6, and it is drawn completely differently: the inkmap shows the vertical passing straight through with a filled blob about 8px wide and 6px tall centred at (461,386) - roughly 3x the 2-3px stroke width in both axes, which is a solder dot (the tracer classes the site kind as 'dot', score 2.5, the highest on the sheet). The contrast between S6 (jog) and S9 (dot) on the same rail is the drafter telling us exactly what they meant. Junction here merges #2's source, #6's drain and both halves of the y~380 rail into n3; the crossing reading would have split n3 into {#2.source, #6.drain} and {#3.source, #5.drain}, both electrically sane, which is why the ink evidence decides it. S1 (273,229), S2 (453,239) CRITICAL -> junction: the drain columns of #3 and #2 end on the top rail as clean T's; a crossing would strand each drain. S10 (231,458) CRITICAL -> junction: #3's gate column ends on the y~462 rail (T). S11 (57,461) CRITICAL -> junction: the y~462 rail ends on the left column between the zener bottom and V-AC #7's top (T). S15 (663,561), S16 (347,580), S17 (475,584), S26 (278,726), S28 (798,734), S29 (653,745), S30 (478,751), S31 (542,753) CRITICAL -> junction: all plain T's where a lead ends on a through wire (resistor into #5's source column, V-AC #10's top into the gate wire, resistor into #6's source column, and the four bottom-rail stubs plus the GND #14 stub, which has a solder blob). Every one of them would strand a terminal if read as a crossing. Non-critical sites left at default: S4 (126,323) is the handwritten '3V' crossing the zener ink (default crossing), S5 (230,324) is the corner of #3's gate lead, S19/S20/S21 (832-846, 669-690) are the '5A'/'3kHz' text brushing the wires near I-AC #11. PORT FIXES: #0 (V-DC 5V) t1 was on port p2@(579,283), a stroke of the handwritten '5V' under the source (one-terminal net); repointed to p3@(596,242), the real right lead that runs right and down into GND #1, so the source's return is on net 0. #4 (Zener 3V) t1 was on p2@(117,342), a stroke of the '3V' label to the right of the symbol (one-terminal net); repointed to p1@(70,279), the real top lead going up to the top rail. #2 (MOSFET-N) had the wrong pin order: the tracer used t1 = p1 (the bottom lead) and t2 = p0 (the left lead). The gate plate is the vertical bar at x~424 and its lead exits bottom-left at (408,323), so ports were set to t0 = p2 (top, drain), t1 = p0 (left, gate), t2 = p1 (bottom, source). #5 (MOSFET-P) is drawn MIRRORED - gate plate on the right at x~705 with its lead leaving to the right at (728,491) - so the tracer's t1 = p1 (bottom) and t2 = p2 (right) were swapped; set to t0 = p0 (top, drain), t1 = p2 (right, gate), t2 = p1 (bottom, source). #3, #6, #12 and #13 already had the right order and were left alone (#12 is also mirrored, gate on the right, and the tracer got it right). DRAIN vs SOURCE: settled from the drawing, not from a convention - in every one of the six symbols the body-arrow lead merges with the BOTTOM lead (visible at x~460 on #2, x~666 on #5, x~470 on #6, x~651 on #12, x~475 on #13), i.e. body tied to source, so the bottom lead is the source and the top lead is the drain in all six. #3 is drawn too small to separate the three right-hand leads in the ink, so it follows the same house style (top = drain, bottom = source); this also agrees with the physical reading since #3's top lead goes to the +5V rail. CLASSES: accepted as annotated. Note for the auditor: the substrate arrow points left (into the channel) on ALL six MOSFETs, including the three labelled MOSFET-P, so the drawing itself does not distinguish N from P here; there is no positive evidence against the annotated classes, so none were changed. The two sine-in-a-circle symbols with an added arrow (#9, #11, labelled '1A 2kHz' and '5A 3kHz') are I-AC and the two without (#7, #10, labelled '1V 2kHz' and '5V 3kHz') are V-AC, which matches the annotation. Remaining warnings are all handwritten text touching a symbol: (546,283) is the '5V' under #0, (117,342)/(118,309) are the '3V' beside the zener, (86,528)/(86,555) are the '1V'/'2kHz' beside V-AC #7 - none is a lead. No bridges dropped (9 exist, none changes the netlist), no merges, no manual nets, nothing unconnected. Result: 15 components, 9 nets, ERC clean.
